gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many full CDs a portable player plays per charge, or whether a car's USB port supplies enough power to keep it playing; for the FiiO DM13 the numbers are 10 h × 60 / 74 min = 8.1 full-length discs per charge, and its average draw of 3.75 Ah × 3.8 V / 10 h = 1.43 W is less than the 2.5 W a USB 2.0 port supplies.
standout_why: Compared against itechguides.com (2026-10-11), ensightauto.com (2026-02-04) and the Walmart, Newegg and manuals.plus results ChatGPT got. Itechguides gives battery hours for generic players (Sunoony 9 h from 2,000 mAh, MEGATEK 15 h from 2,000 mAh). It gives no discs per charge, no power draw and no check against what a car USB port can supply. Ensightauto says power draw is 'similar to charging a phone' but gives no number. None covers the FiiO DM13 or any of our in-dash decks.
decides: This supports the FiiO DM13 BT as the portable pick for cars that have no CD slot. One charge covers about 8 full 74-minute discs. Its average draw at FiiO's test conditions (1.43 W) fits within a USB 2.0 port's 2.5 W, so in principle it can keep playing on the car's USB power. A USB 2.0 port can't reach FiiO's 5 V / 2 A (10 W) charging rate, though, so a full 2.5 h charge needs a 2 A car charger. It does not separate the three in-dash decks: I could not open their RMS power or price pages.

findings.label: Battery
findings.note: Wh worked out from the maker's figures: 3.75 Ah × 3.8 V = 14.25 Wh

findings.label: Rated playback per charge
findings.note: FiiO's test: playing a CD into 3.5 mm headphone out at volume 32, 32 Ω load, display off (4.4 mm: volume 26). FiiO gives no separate figure for Bluetooth transmit mode.

findings.label: Full 74-minute CDs per charge
findings.note: 10 h × 60 min / 74 min = 8.1. The 74-minute Red Book capacity comes from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compact_Disc_Digital_Audio (read 2026-11-17). 80-minute discs: 600 / 80 = 7.5.

findings.label: Average power draw while playing
findings.note: 14.25 Wh / 10 h = 1.43 W, at FiiO's headphone-out, display-off test conditions. Bluetooth transmitting and the screen will raise it.

findings.label: Draw compared with a car USB 2.0 port
findings.value: 1.43 W used of the 2.5 W available (57%)
findings.note: The page gives USB 1.0/2.0 up to 2.5 W and Battery Charging spec up to 7.5 W. 1.43 / 2.5 = 0.57. Ignores conversion losses.

findings.label: Charging requirement and time
findings.value: DC 5 V ≥2 A (10 W); about 2.5 h
findings.note: 10 h of play / 2.5 h of charging = 4 h of play per hour on a 2 A charger. A 2.5 W USB 2.0 port supplies 25% of the rated 10 W input.

findings.label: Line out level (into the car's AUX jack)
findings.note: Copied from the spec sheet; no arithmetic.

findings.label: Rival battery figures (for comparison)
findings.value: Sunoony 9 h from 2,000 mAh; MEGATEK 15 h from 2,000 mAh
findings.source_title: How to Play CDs in a Modern Car: 6 Compatible Options
findings.note: Rival page lists hours only; it gives no discs per charge or watt draw. Converted the same way: 9 h = 7.3 discs and 15 h = 12.2 discs of 74 minutes. These are maker claims the rival repeats, not measurements.
